options.ratio: 1 cup sugar → 3/4 cup grated jaggery. Dissolve it separately and add off the heat, or it will split milk.
options.taste_and_texture: Darker colour, a mineral edge, and a faint smokiness. In a pale dish it will look wrong — in kheer, halwa or a laddu it looks like it should.
options.nutritional_rationale: Carries an iron and mineral fraction that refining removes. Comparable on total sugars — this is not a sugar-reduction swap.

options.ratio: 1 cup sugar → 3/4 cup palm jaggery, or 1 cup soft date paste (reduce the liquid in the recipe by a third).
options.taste_and_texture: Palm jaggery is more caramel and less grassy than cane gur. Date paste browns fast and can catch — it is the worse swap for anything that goes on a hot griddle.
options.nutritional_rationale: Adds fibre in the date version; potassium in the palm version.

where_it_went: Industrial refining and a colonial sugar trade made uniform white sugar cheap and aspirational; jaggery became the rural, second-choice option.
